clinical.citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes (R. Torene et al.)

variants.description: De novo protein-truncating variants in the NMD-escape region (3' end) of HDAC2; specific variant notation not provided
phenotypes: syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo PTV in the NMD-escape region; the gene was significantly enriched for PTVesc DNMs. HDAC2 showed high phenotypic similarity (phenopy) among patients, and is a histone modifier, a known NDD mechanism. Presented as a novel candidate gene.

clinical.citation: ASHG 2015 - Aggregated analysis of developmental disorders reveals novel risk genes and improves genetic diagnosis (K. Retterer et al.)

variants.description: De novo likely gene-disrupting or damaging missense variants in HDAC2; specific variants and patient count not provided
phenotypes: undiagnosed developmental disorder / neurodevelopmental disorder

clinical.diagnostic_reason: HDAC2 was identified as a potentially novel candidate risk gene by aggregated de novo mutation analysis in trios (≥2 LGD or damaging missense de novo variants); proposed mechanism is histone modification.

model_organism.citation: 2025 - HDAC2 enhances the antimicrobial activity of neutrophils by promoting the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in sepsis (PMID: 40850685)
phenotypes: HDAC2 knockout or inhibition reduced inflammation and improved organ function in non-infectious (LPS-induced) sepsis
HDAC2 knockout decreased survival in infectious (CLP) sepsis
Knockout or inhibition significantly reduced NETs formation
Impaired antimicrobial activity against E. coli infection
Mechanism involves H3K18 acetylation and CARM1-mediated H3R17 methylation/citrullination
Dual HDAC2/CARM1 inhibition improved survival in CLP sepsis

model_organism.citation: 2021 - HDAC1/2 Control Proliferation and Survival in Adult Epidermis and Pre-Basal Cell Carcinoma through p16 and p53 (PMID: 34284046)
phenotypes: Epidermal codeletion of Hdac1 and Hdac2 in adult mouse epidermis reduced basal cell proliferation
Increased apoptosis
Inappropriate differentiation
Eventual loss of Hdac1/2-null keratinocytes
Elevated acetylated p53 and increased p16 expression
p53 loss partially restored proliferation; p16 deletion promoted long-term survival of null keratinocytes
In GLI2ΔN-driven pre-basal cell carcinoma, Hdac1/2 deletion reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis

model_organism.citation: 2025 - The deacetylases HDAC1/HDAC2 control JAK2(V617F)-STAT signaling through the ubiquitin ligase SIAH2 (PMID: 40877230)
phenotypes: Genetic depletion of HDAC1/HDAC2 induced apoptosis and long-term growth arrest of JAK2V617F MPN cells in vitro and in vivo
Spared normal hematopoietic stem cells
Did not compromise blood cell differentiation

model_organism.citation: 2019 - Opposite regulation of Wnt/β-catenin and Shh signaling pathways by Rack1 controls mammalian cerebellar development (PMID: 30765517)
phenotypes: Rack1 deletion in NSCs or GNPs caused severe cerebellar morphogenesis defects with impaired folia and fissure formation
Rack1 loss destabilized HDAC1/HDAC2 and reduced Shh signaling
Suppression of HDAC1/HDAC2 activity in the developing cerebellum phenocopied the Rack1 mutant
HDAC2 deficiency in PDAC cells impaired cell cycle progression in vitro
Impaired metastasis formation in vivo, particularly for mesenchymal/undifferentiated PDAC cells
Altered expression of PDGFRα, PDGFRβ and EGFR
Disabled the tumor-suppressive arm of TGFβ signaling

biological.citation: GPR126 regulates colorectal cancer cell proliferation by mediating HDAC2 and GLI2 expression (PMID: 33629464)
biological.summary: GPR126 knockdown reduced HDAC2 transcription and translation in colorectal cancer cells. Ectopic HDAC2 restored viability, proliferation and GLI2 reporter activity, and reduced G1 arrest. HDAC2 regulated GLI2 expression, and HDAC2 and GLI2 both bound the PTCH1 promoter by ChIP, placing HDAC2 in Hedgehog/GLI signaling.

biological.citation: ARHGAP4 regulates the cell migration and invasion of pancreatic cancer by the HDAC2/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 30958531)
biological.summary: ARHGAP4 interacts with and ubiquitinates HDAC2, which inhibits β-catenin activation. The HDAC2 inhibitor CAY10683 and the Wnt inhibitor XAV939 attenuated the effects of ARHGAP4 silencing on invasion and migration, and on MMP2/MMP9 expression, in pancreatic cancer cells. This places HDAC2 in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.

biological.citation: E3 ligase RCHY1 negatively regulates HDAC2 (PMID: 31630802)
biological.summary: RCHY1 directly interacts with HDAC2, and ectopic RCHY1 lowered HDAC2 levels in p53 wild-type, mutant and null cancer cells. RCHY1 knockdown raised HDAC2 levels, and the RING mutant lacked this effect. RCHY1 and HDAC2 levels were inversely correlated in tumor tissue in a meta-analysis of six datasets.

biological.citation: N6-methyladenosine-modified SENP1, identified by IGF2BP3, ... activating AKT signal via de-SUMOylating HDAC2 (PMID: 38822351)
biological.summary: Co-IP showed SENP1 binds HDAC2 in AML cells, and SENP1 de-SUMOylates HDAC2. This enhances EGFR transcription (ChIP-qPCR) and activates AKT/mTOR signaling, promoting AML proliferation and anti-apoptosis.

biological.citation: HDAC2 Induces DNA Methyltransferase DNMT3B Expression to Regulate the Wnt Signaling Pathway and Thus Promotes Glioma Development and Progression (PMID: 36267089)
biological.summary: ChIP showed HDAC2 is enriched on the DNMT3B promoter and activates its transcription. DNMT3B in turn represses Bcl2 and promotes Wnt pathway activity. HDAC2 and DNMT3B are highly expressed in glioma and associated with poor prognosis, and the axis promotes glioma activity in vitro and in vivo.

biological.citation: MiR-646 prevents proliferation and progression of human breast cancer cell lines by suppressing HDAC2 expression (PMID: 32777446)
biological.summary: HDAC2 was significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent non-cancerous tissue and a normal cell line. miR-646 directly targets HDAC2. HDAC2 knockout or miR-646 overexpression inhibited growth and promoted cell death.
biological.sample_size: 30 tumor/30 adjacent normal tissues; 3 breast cancer cell lines

biological.citation: Inactivation of HDAC1 or HDAC2 induces gamma globin expression without altering cell cycle or proliferation (PMID: 25808664)
biological.summary: shRNA knockdown of HDAC2 or HDAC1 in human erythroid progenitors induced gamma globin without changing proliferation or cell cycle. HDAC2 knockdown combined with hydroxyurea gave a further increase in gamma globin. The HDAC1/2/3 inhibitor MS-275 was additive with hydroxyurea in CD34+ cells.

biological.citation: Neural stem cell differentiation is dictated by distinct actions of nuclear receptor corepressors and histone deacetylases (PMID: 25241747)
biological.summary: Genome-wide analysis showed HDAC2 and HDAC3 have overlapping and distinct promoter occupancy at neuronal and oligodendrocyte genes in neural stem cells. HDAC2 directly represses Sox8 and Sox10. Loss of HDAC2 or NCOR with T3 increased oligodendrocyte gene expression, whereas HDAC3 loss, but not HDAC2 loss, initiated neuronal differentiation.

biological.citation: YTHDC1 is downregulated by the YY1/HDAC2 complex and controls the sensitivity of ccRCC to sunitinib by targeting the ANXA1-MAPK pathway (PMID: 35974388)
biological.summary: HDAC2 acts in a YY1/HDAC2 complex that downregulates YTHDC1 in ccRCC, defining a YY1/HDAC2/YTHDC1/ANXA1 axis. HDAC2 inhibitors resensitized ccRCC cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as sunitinib.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes
biological.summary: Two patients with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder carried de novo NMD-escaping protein-truncating variants in HDAC2. HDAC2 was identified as a candidate novel disease gene, consistent with histone modifiers being a known NDD mechanism.
